bull.b: The long-term Anthropic lease provides substantial contracted revenue visibility and expands TeraWulf’s relationship with a major AI customer. This supports the transition toward recurring HPC infrastructure income, reduces reliance on bitcoin mining economics, and can underpin future financing and capacity investment.

Rapid growth in HPC lease revenue shows that the business is developing a meaningful recurring infrastructure segment alongside mining. Rising contribution from leases can improve revenue quality over time, while additional Lake Mariner capacity creates a pathway for further operating scale.

Securing up to 1 GW of contracted power at Muskie strengthens TeraWulf’s access to large-scale energy for AI and high-performance computing development. The expanded platform increases strategic capacity, supports customer growth, and reinforces the company’s power-advantaged infrastructure positioning.

bear.b: Gross profit has not translated into sustainable operating or net earnings, with the latest trailing period showing an exceptionally large net loss relative to revenue. Continued losses could constrain internally funded growth and leave results vulnerable to cost overruns, financing needs, or accounting volatility.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow indicates that the core business is not currently self-funding its expansion. Combined with very high leverage relative to equity, this increases dependence on financing and asset monetization while reducing flexibility if project spending or debt-service demands remain elevated.

Pre-revenue costs, constrained electrical labor, and customer-driven design complexity are weighing on near-term profitability and schedule execution. Although contracted capacity is growing, reported margins remain well below the long-term target, creating a risk that scaling projects consume cash before contributing expected earnings.
